We are looking for composers who take their craft seriously.



Not bedroom producers chasing trends. Not beatmakers looking to crossover. Composers who have dedicated themselves to the art of cinematic music — who understand orchestration, dynamics, tension, emotion, and how music serves a picture.



If that is you — keep reading.



Who We Are



Rareform Audio and Black Sheep Music are a music and audio post production house specializing in music for movie trailers, ads, film, and TV. Rareform Production Music is our production music imprint — built to deliver world class cinematic music across a wide range of styles and moods. We hold ourselves to an obsessive standard of excellence and we only work with composers who feel the same way.



The Role



We are building our composer roster and looking for talented cinematic composers to collaborate with on a per project basis. You will be given briefs, creative direction, and album concepts — and your job is to deliver high quality, professionally mixed and mastered cues that are ready for placement. We may have full time positions open as well for composers who are a good match.



We are not looking for one sound. We are looking for composers who are versatile and can move across styles — but we also understand that everyone has their strengths and specialties. We are open to finding where you fit best within our catalog and our team.



Styles We Are Looking For



- Orchestral mockups and hybrid cinematic scores

- Action, thriller, and tension driven cues

- Horror and dark atmospheric music

- Emotional piano and string suites

- Percussive and rhythmic cinematic cues

- Epic and uplifting cinematic music



You do not need to do all of these. But the more range you have the more opportunities we can bring your way.



What We're Looking For



- A genuine cinematic composer — not a beatmaker or hip hop producer looking to crossover

- Able to write, arrange, mix, and master to a professional standard and deliver broadcast ready cues

- Strong understanding of orchestration and how to build dynamics, tension, and emotion

- Versatile across multiple cinematic styles and moods

- Self directed and able to deliver on brief with minimal back and forth

- Reliable — deadlines are real and we need composers who honor them

- Open to creative direction and feedback without taking it personally



Important Attributes We Hire For



We build our roster around infinite learners, self-directed problem solvers, and people with high standards of excellence. If you hold yourself to a high bar because that is just who you are — not because someone is watching — you will fit here.



This Is NOT For You If



- Your background is primarily hip hop, pop, or beat production with no cinematic experience

- You cannot mix and master your own work to a professional standard

- You struggle to deliver on brief or need excessive direction

- You are not reliable with deadlines

- Your demo reel does not speak for itself



How to Apply



Submit your demo reel or portfolio links in the form below — this is the most important part of your application and will be reviewed first.



Also record a short Loom video (2–3 minutes) and paste the link in the form. In your video tell us:



1. Who you are and what your background as a composer looks like

2. Where your strengths lie — what styles and sounds you do best

3. Where your weaknesses are — what styles you are still developing or don't feel as natural in



That last question matters to us. We are not looking for someone who claims to do everything perfectly. We are looking for someone self aware enough to know their craft deeply — strengths and all.



Applications without a demo reel will not be reviewed.

title: Music Coordinator
description:
Jobe Code: 260404E_Music Coordinator (RAxBSM)

Full-Time | Remote | LA Hours Required



Please note that our account here is only active for a limited time. After that, we won't be able to respond to messages and our links will be deactivated. If you're coming across this after the fact, search for Rareform Audio online and reach out to us directly through our website.



Also, please follow our specific application instructions below. If an applicant misses the steps, it raises concerns about attention to detail and fit for the role.



Who We Are



Rareform Audio and Black Sheep Music are a combined music and audio post production house specializing in music for movie trailers, ads, film, and TV. We create music for the biggest campaigns in the world and we take that seriously. We are a small, tight-knit team of A-players who hold ourselves to an obsessive standard of excellence. We don't half-ass anything. We don't cut corners. And we don't settle for good enough when great is possible.

We are looking for someone who feels the same way.



We are looking for someone who feels the same way.



The Role



This is not a basic admin job. This is for someone whose dream is to become a music supervisor — and who wants to start building that career for real, right now.



Trailer music is one of our main lanes and one of the most competitive spaces in the music for media industry. When a brief comes in there is no partial credit. The playlist either stops someone in their tracks or it gets passed over. You are the person sitting at that 
nt — determining whether our music finds a home or gets lost in the noise. That is not a small thing and we need someone who feels the weight of it.



Music has to live in you. You think in it, speak it, feel when something is right and when it isn't. The strongest candidates for this role tend to be composers and producers — people who have spent years making music and developing a deep understanding of how it works emotionally, sonically, and structurally. That background is not required but it is a serious advantage. If you are a composer or producer who has always found yourself gravitating toward curation — building playlists, matching music to 
nts, obsessing over what fits and what doesn't — you may have just found your lane.



You won't come in with industry experience. You'll come in with an obsessive musical mind, a hunger to become one of the best in the world at this, and the drive to learn fast. We will invest in the right person. Over time this role grows into a Head of Operations position.



If you are sharp, self-directed, obsessed with music, and wired to make things happen — keep reading.



What You'll Do



- Receive client briefs and curate playlists from our catalog that match the vibe, emotion, and style of each request

- Decode what clients are asking for — sometimes reading between the lines to find the right direction

- Coordinate custom music requests — matching the right composer to the right project based on style, availability, and timeline

- Handle stem requests and instrumental deliveries

- Manage project communication and keep things moving without needing to be micromanaged

- Grow into catalog mastery so that briefs can eventually be handled end-to-end

- Identify patterns in briefs over time and d
 what new music we should create



What We're Looking For



- A genuine love for trailer music — you know the genre, the styles, and what makes a cue land

- Exceptional written English — you will be communicating directly with clients and your writing needs to be polished and professional

- Available on Los Angeles time — briefs are time-sensitive and we need you present during business hours

- Self-directed and proactive — you figure things out, you don't wait to be told every step

- OCD-level organization and attention to detail

- High integrity — this role comes with access to our full client relationships and catalog

- An A-player mentality — you hold yourself to a high standard because that's just who you are, not because someone is watching



Important Attributes We Hire For



We built our team around people who are infinite learners, self-directed problem solvers, trustworthy, driven, accountable, and high energy. If those words describe you naturally, you will fit here. If you need to be pushed to meet a basic standard, this is not the right place.



This Role Is NOT For You If



- You need step-by-step instructions for everything

- You are not genuinely passionate about music and the trailer music world

- Your English communication is anything less than excellent

- You are looking for a quiet, easy job with minimal responsibility



How to Apply



To apply, please record a short Loom video (3–5 minutes maximum) and paste the link in the form below. We want to hear you think out loud about music — this is the most important part of your application.



In your video, cover these three things:



1. Put us in your world. Walk us through the last piece of music that genuinely stopped you. Not what you think sounds impressive — the thing that actually hit you. Describe what it's doing sonically and emotionally in as much detail as you can. We want to hear how you think and speak about music.



2.  Show us your curatorial instinct. You've just received a brief — a high octane action thriller trailer, building from tension to full chaos, needs to feel dangerous and cinematic. Without looking anything up, tell us the direction you'd go musically. Style, energy, instrumentation, tempo, what it feels like. Walk us through your thinking.



3. Tell us why you're built for this. Not why you want it — why you're the right person. What in your background, your obsessions, your skills, makes you someone we should bet on to grow into this role.



Applications without a Loom video will not be reviewed. Generic answers will not move forward. We are looking for someone who already thinks this way — not someone who can research the right answer.



Apply here: 



Again, please note that our account here is only active for a limited time. After that, we won't be able to respond to messages and our links will be deactivated. If you're coming across this after the fact, search for Rareform Audio online and reach out to us directly through our website.

title: Admin Assistant (Music & Operations)
description:
Job Code
B_Admin Assistant (Music & Operations)



Please note that our account here is only active for a limited time. After that, we won't be able to respond to messages and our links will be deactivated. If you're coming across this after the fact, search for Rareform Audio online and reach out to us directly through our website.



Also, please follow our specific application instructions below. If an applicant misses the steps, it raises concerns about attention to detail and fit for the role.



This role is for someone who figures things out.



Not someone who needs their hand held through every task. Not someone who asks the same question three times. Someone who receives a quick video walkthrough, asks any questions if needed, and then goes and gets it done right the first time.



If that's how your brain works — keep reading.



Who We Are



Rareform Audio and Black Sheep Music are a combined music and audio post production house specializing in music for movie trailers, ads, film, and TV. We create music for the biggest campaigns in the world and we hold ourselves to an obsessive standard of excellence. We don't half-ass anything and we don't settle for good enough when great is possible.



The Role (20-40 hours per week)



This is a support role that requires a sharp, trustworthy, and highly adaptable person. Our world moves fast and the tasks are rarely the same twice. You will receive direction — often via a quick video walkthrough — and your job is to take it from there. 



Getting things wrong in a music catalog environment is not a minor inconvenience. It creates real damage. We need someone who understands that accuracy and attention to detail are non-negotiable, and who takes that responsibility seriously without needing to be reminded.



What You'll Do



- Update and manage song metadata across our music catalog

- Handle music catalog requests and management tasks

- Assist with client outreach and communications

- Weekly LinkedIn connection building and outreach

- Handle miscellaneous payment and finance related tasks

- Pick up new tasks quickly as they arise — this list will grow and change



What We're Looking For



- Sheer intelligence and the ability to pick things up fast

- Exceptional attention to detail — especially when working with catalog data

- Strong written English — clear, professional communication at all times

- Trustworthy and dependable — you will have access to sensitive catalog and financial information

- A problem solver who figures things out rather than waiting to be told every step

- Proactive communicator — if something is unclear you ask once, smartly, then move forward

- Comfortable with ambiguity — not every task will come with a detailed manual



Important Attributes We Hire For



We build our team around infinite learners, self-directed problem solvers, and people with high standards of excellence. Trustworthy, driven, accountable, and high energy. If those words describe you naturally you will fit here. If you need to be micromanaged or reminded to follow through this is not the right place.



This Role Is NOT For You If



- You need step-by-step instructions for every task every time

- Attention to detail is not your strong suit

- You are not comfortable working with music catalog data and administrative systems

- You need a lot of back and forth before getting things done

- You treat mistakes as no big deal



How to Apply



Record a short Loom video (2–3 minutes) and paste the link in the form below. 



- Tell us about a time you had to figure something out on your own with minimal guidance — what was the situation, what did you do, and what was the result.

- Show us something you've built. A product, a system, a page, a track, a brand, a process — anything. Show us what you're capable of and tell us why you're proud of it.

- Then tell us why this role is the right fit for you right now.



Applications without a Loom video will not be reviewed.



Apply here:

title: Customer Success & Implementation Specialist — B2B SaaS, Go High Level Required
description:
Full-Time | Remote — Philippines Only | U.S. Pacific-Time Night Shift



Compensation



?60,000–?75,000 monthly base, depending on experience



Plus:



* Up to ?15,000 monthly performance incentive

* Up to ?15,000 quarterly excellence bonus

* Compensation review after successful completion of the introductory period

* Long-term advancement opportunity into Senior Customer Success Manager or Head of Implementation



Do not apply if your expected base compensation falls outside the stated range.



Schedule



Monday–Friday

6:00 AM–3:00 PM United States Pacific Time



This generally corresponds to:



* 9:00 PM–6:00 AM Philippine Time while California is on daylight-saving time

* 10:00 PM–7:00 AM Philippine Time while California is on standard time



The selected candidate must have a reliable home office and be consistently available during the complete assigned shift.



?



About GuardGrade



GuardGrade is an early-stage B2B SaaS platform being built for the private-security industry.



Security companies produce operational evidence every day through Daily Activity Reports, patrol documentation, i
 reports, staffing information, and other records. GuardGrade ingests this information and turns it into structured, explainable performance intelligence across three levels:



* GuardScore: individual observed guard-performance and reliability patterns

* SiteScore: performance within the operating conditions of a specific security site

* VendorScore: security-company service delivery, supervision, and management patterns



GuardGrade also includes vendor profiles, a security-company directory, client accounts, site onboarding, reporting workflows, and performance dashboards.



The platform is currently entering real-world pilot deployment. We are hiring our first dedicated Customer Success and Implementation Specialist to help customers deploy successfully, remain active, and receive fast, organized support.



?



Mission of the role



Your mission is:



Ensure every qualified GuardGrade customer moves from signup to successful, active use without becoming confused, stalled, or ignored.



This is not a passive support role.



You will not simply wait for tickets.



You will proactively monitor onboarding, identify stalled accounts, communicate with customers, coordinate product issues, maintain accurate CRM records, and help GuardGrade improve based on real customer behavior.



You will work directly with:



* The CEO

* The CTO and development team

* The GoHighLevel/automation team

* Security-company owners and operations managers

* Client-side users

* Future sales and marketing staff



?



Core responsibilities



1. Customer onboarding and implementation



You will guide new companies through:



* Vendor-account creation

* Client-account creation

* Company-profile completion

* Internal-user invitations

* Site setup

* Site Context setup

* Guard/user setup where required

* Unique DAR
 configuration

* First DAR submission

* Confirmation that reports were processed

* Dashboard review

* Initial scoring-readiness review

* Customer launch confirmation



You will maintain an implementation checklist for every account and ensure no critical step is skipped.



2. Proactive customer-success management



You will monitor:



* New signups

* Claim-started but incomplete profiles

* Claimed profiles that have not activated

* Vendors without sites

* Sites without incoming DARs

* Inactive or stale accounts

* Unresolved customer questions

* Customers at risk of abandoning onboarding

* Repeated customer friction

* Accounts ready for expansion or additional sites



You must contact customers before inactivity becomes churn.



3. GoHighLevel ownership



You must be able to work confidently inside GoHighLevel.



Responsibilities include:



* Updating contacts, companies, opportunities, and custom fields

* Moving opportunities accurately through pipelines

* Reviewing workflow status and contact history

* Creating tasks and follow-up reminders

* Managing conversations across
, SMS, calls, and chat

* Checking whether automation fired correctly

* Identifying duplicate records

* Applying correct tags and lifecycle fields

* Understanding triggers, filters, wait steps, branches, and suppression logic

* Testing forms, calendars, campaigns, workflows, and notifications

* Escalating automation failures clearly to the automation team

* Maintaining clean CRM notes and customer records



You are not expected to be the lead automation engineer, but you must understand GHL well enough to inspect workflows, recognize failures, conduct QA, and communicate precisely with technical staff.



4. Customer communication



You will conduct:



* Video onboarding calls

* Follow-up calls

*
 support

* Chat and CRM conversations

* Account-health check-ins

* Weekly pilot follow-ups

* Training sessions

* Basic product demonstrations



You must communicate professionally with U.S.-based business owners and operations executives.



You must be comfortable explaining technical processes in plain English without sounding scripted or robotic.



5. Support triage



You will classify incoming issues as:



* How-to question

* Account/configuration problem

* DAR-ingestion problem

* Product defect

* AI extraction issue

* Scoring question

* Verification/profile issue

* Billing issue

* Feature request

* Privacy, legal, reputational, or sensitive complaint



You must know what you can solve and what must be escalated.



You may not independently:



* Change scores

* Promise score improvements

* Resolve formal score disputes

* Make legal claims

* Guarantee future performance

* Tell customers that payment improves scoring

* Invent an answer when documentation is incomplete



6. Bug and product-feedback reporting



Weak report:



“The customer says it doesn’t work.”



Required report:



* Customer/company

* Site or account

* User

* Date/time

* Reproduction steps

* Expected result

* Actual result

* Screenshot/video

* Relevant DAR or record

* Severity

* Business impact

* Temporary workaround

* Whether the issue is recurring



You will maintain organized records of:



* Bugs

* Product friction

* Feature requests

* Common questions

* Lost or stalled customers

* Customer objections

* Requested integrations

* Documentation gaps



7. Training and documentation



You will help build and maintain:



* Customer onboarding guides

* Internal SOPs

* Help-center articles

* FAQs

* Short training videos

* Loom walkthroughs

* Troubleshooting guides

* Standard customer responses

* Implementation checklists

* Pilot surveys

* Release-update explanations



Documentation must be clear enough that another employee can follow it without asking what you meant.



8. Customer-health reporting



You will assign and maintain customer-health states:



* Onboarding

* Healthy

* Attention Needed

* At Risk

* Recovery

* Churned



Every business day, you must know:



* Who is onboarding

* Who is blocked

* Who is inactive

* Who needs human intervention

* Which issue is preventing progress

* What the next action is

* Who owns that action

* When it is due



?



Daily operating rhythm



Start of shift



Review:



* New signups and profile claims

* New customer messages

* Open onboarding accounts

* Stalled implementations

* Failed or missing DAR activity

* Overnight product/automation alerts

* Open tickets and engineering responses

Create a prioritized task list:



1. Customer-blocking issues

2. New onboarding

3. At-risk accounts

4. Open support

5. Documentation and process improvement



First half of shift



* Respond to urgent questions

* Conduct onboarding calls

* Follow up with stalled customers

* Verify implementation steps

* Test reported issues

* Escalate product defects

* Update GHL and implementation records



Second half of shift



* Conduct training or account-health calls

* Review inactive accounts

* Update documentation

* Follow up with engineering

* Prepare customer updates

* Complete quality checks

* Confirm next actions



End of shift



Submit a short written report containing:



* Customers onboarded

* Customers blocked

* Major issues

* Bugs escalated

* At-risk accounts

* Customer feedback

* Actions needed from the CTO

* Actions needed from the CEO

* Priorities for the next shift



This report should be concise and decision-oriented—not a diary of every task completed.



?



Required qualifications



Applicants must meet all core requirements.



GoHighLevel



* At least one year of practical GoHighLevel experience, or substantial equivalent project experience

* Must have personally worked with pipelines, opportunities, custom fields, workflows, forms, calendars, conversations, tasks, tags, triggers, filters, and automation QA

* Must be able to explain one GHL workflow you personally built or managed

* Must understand how to prevent contradictory workflows and duplicate communication

* Must understand the difference between a CRM field, tag, pipeline stage, task, and workflow state



Candidates whose only GHL experience is watching tutorials should not apply.



Customer success / implementation



* At least two years in one or more of the following:

    * SaaS customer success

    * Software implementation

    * Technical account management

    * B2B onboarding

    * CRM implementation

    * Technology customer support

* Experience managing multiple customer implementations simultaneously

* Experience conducting live customer calls

* Experience following up proactively with inactive users

* Experience documenting product issues for developers



Communication



* Excellent spoken and written English

* Clear, confident video-call presence

* Ability to communicate with executives and operations staff

* Ability to simplify software instructions

* Strong active-listening skills

* Ability to remain calm with confused or frustrated customers

* No fear of making professional outbound follow-up calls



Technical and operational ability



* Strong attention to detail

* Strong troubleshooting mindset

* Comfortable learning an unfamiliar SaaS product

* Able to reproduce problems before escalating them

* Able to distinguish user error, configuration error, automation failure, and product defect

* Comfortable working with Google Workspace, spreadsheets, Loom, ticketing/project-management systems, and CRM tools

* Basic understanding of APIs, webhooks, integrations, and automation logic is strongly preferred

* Familiarity with n8n, Make, Zapier, Stripe, AI tools, or support platforms is a major advantage



Work environment



* Stable high-speed internet

* Backup internet connection

* Reliable computer capable of video calls and multiple browser applications

* Quiet, professional workspace

* Functional headset and webcam

* Reliable power or realistic backup-power plan

* Ability to work the complete Pacific-Time night schedule

* No conflicting full-time role

* Must be willing to use time tracking and attend scheduled tea
etings



?



Behavioral requirements



We want someone who:



* Takes ownership rather than waits for instructions

* Notices when customers stop progressing

* Follows through until an issue is resolved

* Documents accurately

* Does not hide mistakes

* Asks precise questions

* Does not guess when uncertain

* Pushes back professionally when a process is broken

* Cares about customer outcomes, not ticket volume

* Can work in an early-stage company where processes are still being built

* Is comfortable with change, feedback, and accountability

* Can distinguish urgency from noise



Do not apply if you need every task defined before taking action.



?



Preferred qualifications



Strong preference will be given to applicants with experience in:



* Early-stage B2B SaaS

* GoHighLevel SaaS mode

* CRM and automation agencies

* Software implementation

* Customer-health tracking

* Onboarding U.S. businesses

* Voice, SMS, and
 automation

* AI-enabled SaaS products

* GHL snapshots and subaccounts

* Building SOPs and knowledge bases

* Working directly with developers

* Security, facilities, property management, or field-service industries



Private-security experience is helpful but not mandatory. We can teach the industry. We cannot quickly teach ownership, communication discipline, and SaaS implementation maturity.



?



Performance expectations



First 30 days



The selected candidate should be able to:



* Learn GuardGrade’s vendor and client workflows

* Navigate relevant GHL pipelines and records

* Conduct supervised onboarding

* Maintain accurate implementation checklists

* Submit high-quality bug reports

* Produce initial FAQ/SOP improvements

* Demonstrate reliable attendance and communication



By 60 days



* Independently run standard onboarding calls

* Own customer follow-up

* Identify stalled accounts without being prompted

* Resolve common issues

* Maintain account health

* Coordinate effectively with the CTO and automation team

* Improve onboarding documentation



By 90 days



* Own routine customer implementation end to end

* Maintain predictable onboarding performance

* Provide actionable weekly customer-intelligence reports

* Reduce founder involvement in routine onboarding/support

* Demonstrate readiness for expanded account ownership



?



Performance incentives



Bonuses should reward customer outcomes without encouraging cheating.



Monthly target bonus: up to ?15,000



1. Onboarding execution — up to ?4,000



Measured by:



* Qualified customers reaching agreed activation milestones

* Accurate implementation documentation

* Reasonable implementation speed

* No false stage advancement



2. Customer responsiveness and resolution — up to ?3,000



Measured by:



* Response-time compliance

* Follow-up completion

* Customer-blocking issues escalated quickly

* Clear communication during unresolved i



3. Customer-health discipline — up to ?3,000



Measured by:



* Accurate health statuses

* At-risk accounts identified early

* Recovery actions documented

* No customer silently abandoned



4. CRM and documentation quality — up to ?3,000



Measured by:



* Accurate GHL records

* Complete notes

* No duplicate or misleading lifecycle states

* Useful SOP/help-center improvements



5. Customer feedback and quality — up to ?2,000



Measured by:



* Customer satisfaction

* Call-quality reviews

* Positive qualitative feedback

* No substantiated complaints involving dishonesty or neglect



Quarterly excellence bonus: up to ?15,000



Awarded for exceptional results such as:



* Meaningful onboarding-process improvement

* High-impact documentation

* Recovering strategically important at-risk customers

* Identifying a systemic product issue before it harms multiple customers

Non-negotiable bonus rule



No bonus based solely on:

Those metrics are easy to game.



Quality, adoption, accuracy, and customer outcomes matter.

title: Graphic Designer
description:
ABOUT EPYC MEDIA

EPYC Media is a cultural storytelling agency known for building network ready content ecosystems for culturally influential founders, brands, athletes, entertainers, non profits, and enterprises. We believe story comes before format, emotional resonance creates audience loyalty, and premium production is a form of respect for the audience. The best content doesn't interrupt culture, it becomes part of it. Most of our team has been with EPYC 5+ years, because the work asks a lot of you (real detail, real craft, real effort) but it also moves the needle.



THE ROLE

EPYC is scaling its visual output across a growing network of premium podcast and docuseries clients, and we need a second high-level creative eye to help carry that volume without compromising the polish our brand is known for. This is not a production-line design job; it's the first impression that gets someone to click play, and the visual language that keeps a show feeling premium episode after episode. You'll work directly with our Lead Graphic Designer and the Post Production team to translate raw footage, story arcs, and brand identities into graphics that feel cinematic, intentional, and culturally fluent, never templated, never stock, never cheap.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

YouTube Thumbnails: high-CTR, on-brand, story-forward, never clickbait-generic.

Reel Covers + Copy: strong visual composition paired with sharp, voice-accurate copywriting.

Podcast Cover Art: full show identity development across new and existing shows.

Story & Segment Graphics: lower thirds, quote cards, carousel/swipe graphics, IG Stories assets.

Show-to-Show Consistency: maintaining each client's distinct brand system across high-volume output.

Cross-Team Collaboration: working with editors and QA so graphics land in sync with edit timing and deadlines.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Strong creative instincts: able to take a loose brief (or a gut-feeling direction) and turn it into something premium and story-first.

Social performance experience: thumbnails, covers, and reels that drive click-through without going tabloid.

Multi-brand fluency: comfortable working across several client identities at once, with zero visual bleed between shows.

Copywriting instinct: punchy, culturally aware, on-voice text for reels and graphics.

Reliable turnaround on high-volume deliverables without sacrificing quality.



SOFTWARE

Adobe Illustrator: required.

Adobe Photoshop: required, heavy daily use.

Canva: proficient, used for fast-turnaround and templated systems.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within 90 days, you're fully embedded in EPYC's design pipeline, producing thumbnails, covers, and story graphics independently across multiple client shows. Your work should be indistinguishable in quality from our Lead Graphic Designer's, giving the design function room to grow into EPYC's next stage.

title: Sales Data & Reporting Auditor
description:
Why This Role Exists



Zion currently manages ~15 sales reps across multiple offers while also running recruiting, interviews, call reviews, and data integrity. Data integrity is the piece with the lowest skill ceiling and the highest time cost.



Per Josh's Framework 6 (Pipeline Management), this is a named, separate seat for a reason:



Josh once had sales managers audit the CRM daily — chasing reps for missed forms, unmarked show-ups, blank fields. It completely destroyed his capacity model for sales management. The fix was a dedicated CRM Admin owning the tech and data side, so managers spend 30 minutes in the CRM and know everything is where it's supposed to be.



The purpose of this role is to protect the sales manager's capacity. Every hour it buys back gets redeployed into call reviews, rep coaching, and client acquisition — the things that actually move revenue.



The Two Audit Paths



Every issue this person finds falls into one of two buckets. They are handled differently. This distinction is the entire job.



Path 1 — Data Accuracy ? the Auditor fixes it



Data that is wrong or missing because of a system gap, not a rep behavior problem.

- Booked call on the calendar with no lead source attribution.

-Lead in CRM with no meeting date attached.

-Duplicate leads or duplicate calendar events

-Calendar event missing setter initials

-Disposition logged but revenue field blank

-Timezone or date errors on booked calls



Action: fix it directly, log it in the daily report as a count.



Path 2 — Rep Non-Compliance ? the Auditor tags, never cleans

-Data that is wrong because a rep didn't do their job.

-Call happened, no disposition logged

-Show / no-show never marked

-Post-call form not completed

-Lead marked lost with no attempt history

-Deal closed with no payment terms entered

-

Action: tag the rep, create the task, escalate in the daily report.  Do not fix it for them.



Non-negotiable, per Josh: "CRM admins audit — they don't clean. Cleaners create lazy reps."



The 
nt reps learn someone downstream cleans up after them, compliance collapses permanently and the data problem becomes structural. The Auditor's job on Path 2 is to make non-compliance visible, not invisible.



Daily Responsibilities



Morning — booked call audit (start of day)Pull every call on the calendar for the current day and produce:



1. Total booked calls today, by closer

2. Source attribution on every booked call — Ads (self-booked) / Phone Setter / DM Setter / Triage / Reschedule / Referral

3. Setter attribution by initials on every setter-sourced call

4. Confirmation status per the calendar color convention:

          Unmarked = unconfirmed

          Red = no answer

          Yellow = text confirmation received

          Light green = same-day confirmation received

5. Exception list — every call with no confirmation touch at all. This is the highest-value output of the morning report. Every unconfirmed call is a booked call at risk, and it is actionable before the call, not after.



End of day — outcome audit

1. Live calls (showed) vs. booked calls, by closer and by setter.

2. Show rate for the day, and rolling 7-day

3. No-shows and cancellations, with reschedule status: rescheduled / attempted, not reached / no attempt made

4. "No attempt made" list — every no-show nobody has touched. Escalate by name.

5. Missing dispositions — every call with no outcome logged, tagged to the rep.

6. Cash collected logged against calls, where applicable



Weekly — rollup

1. Show rate by setter, trended

2. Booked calls by source, trended — which channel is actually producing.

3. Data-accuracy issue counts by type, trended (are the same issues recurring?).

4. Rep non-compliance counts, by rep name



Metrics This Role Owns



Metrics & Definition:



Booked calls / day = Total on calendar, by closer

Source attribution % = % of booked calls with a source recorded. Target: 100%

Confirmation coverage = % of tomorrow's calls with a confirmation touch logged

Live calls / day = Calls that showed

Show rate = Live ÷ booked, daily and rolling 7-day

Reschedule capture rate = % of no-shows with a documented reschedule attempt

Disposition compliance = % of completed calls with an outcome logged

Data accuracy issues = Count found, count fixed, by category



Show rate belongs to the setter and confirmation layer. It is never a closer metric. This role reports it against setters, not closers.



Explicitly NOT This Role

- Not a sales role. 

- No dialing, no setting, no closing, no prospect contact.

- Not a call reviewer. Call quality grading stays with Zion.

- Not a coach. They report data on reps. They never give reps feedback or direction.

- Not a cleaner for rep non-compliance. See Path 2 above.

- Not the person who d
 what the numbers mean. They report accurately and flag anomalies. Interpretation and action are Zion's.



Required Skills:

-Must have



- High-volume, detail-heavy data work with near-zero error tolerance

- CRM competence — Close CRM strongly preferred; HubSpot / Salesforce / GHL acceptable

- Google Sheets: pivot tables, lookups, conditional formatting

- Google Calendar

- Slack

- Written English clear enough to write a report a manager reads in 60 seconds

Overlap with US Eastern business hours



Nice to have

- Zapier or Make

- Experience inside a sales team (understands what a booked call, show rate, and disposition actually are)

- Prior audit or QA role



Disqualifying

- Needs to be told the same thing twice

- Reports numbers without flagging when a number looks wrong



Reporting Cadence



When - What - Where



Daily, by 9:00 AM ET - Morning booked-call audit + unconfirmed exception list - Slack

Daily, within 30 min of last call - EOD outcome audit + no-attempt list - Slack

Weekly, Monday AM - Rolling rollup - Slack + Sheet



Format requirement: every report is scannable in under 60 seconds. Number first, exception list second, everything else omitted. Nobody reads a wall of data — the exception list is the product.



30-Day Ramp



Week 1 — observe and document



Shadow the current manual process. Document it as they learn it — that document becomes the role's SOP and its first deliverable.



Week 2 — morning report only



Own the morning booked-call audit. Zion verifies against source data daily. Accuracy before scope.



Week 3 — add EOD report



Both daily reports running. Auditor begins flagging Path 1 data-accuracy issues and fixing them.



Week 4 — full scope



Weekly rollup added. Path 2 rep tagging goes live. Zion spot-checks weekly instead of daily.



Ramp gate: the role is not considered ramped until Zion has spot-checked a full week of reports against source data and found zero discrepancies. Wrong data is worse than no data — it produces confidently wrong decisions.



Documentation Requirement



Every process this person runs gets documented as they run it, not after. By day 30 there should be a complete SOP covering: where each number is pulled from, how each is calculated, the report template, and the escalation path for each issue type.



Per Josh: document while doing, not before delegating. If this person leaves, the replacement should be productive in a week off the SOP alone. The right sequence: hire this person to run it manually and document the exact logic while doing it. That documentation becomes the automation spec. Once the reports are automated, the role shifts from producing the data to auditing it — which is the seat Josh actually describes, and it scales.



Hire for the manual work. Scope the job so it produces the automation.



How to Apply

To be considered for this role, you must include the word "Sesquipedalian" in your
 subject line or within the very first sentence of your message. Applications lacking "Sesquipedalian" will automatically be skipped out.



We are reviewing applications on a rolling, fast-track basis to fill this seat immediately with the right candidate. Qualified applicants will receive prompt outreach for an initial interview.

This person is the primary point of contact for every client booking a party or event at Highland House, and is expected to deliver white-glove, luxury hospitality at every touchpoint. Families booking with us expect a premium, seamless experience comparable to a high-end hotel or private event service — this role sets that tone from the first
 to the final thank-you note.

 Event Contact — White-Glove Hospitality



- Serve as the primary, dedicated point of contact for every party/event booking, start to finish, with a warm, polished, concierge-level tone in every interaction

- Respond to party inquiries promptly (same-day) and with a personal touch, not a form-letter feel

- Guide families through package selection, add-ons, and scheduling with genuine care and attentiveness to what makes each celebration special

- Be present and visible on party day to personally check in with the host family, anticipate needs, and smooth over any issues before the client even notices them

- Handle rescheduling, cancellations, and any day-of issues gracefully and calmly, as the client's single point of contact

- Send a personal follow-up/thank-you after every event to reinforce the premium experience



### Party Documents



- Build and maintain all party-related documents: booking contracts, deposit/payment agreements, party-day checklists, host run-of-show sheets, and post-party follow-up materials

- Keep documents organized and current in Notion, so the whole team can find and use them

- Create standardized templates so every party runs the same high-quality way regardless of who's hosting





Pricing Guide



- Build and maintain a clear, up-to-date pricing guide covering all packages and add-ons

- Keep pricing consistent across the website, PDFs, and any client-facing materials

- Flag when pricing needs review (seasonal changes, new add-ons, cost increases



Images & Visual Assets



- Source, organize, and maintain photos/images representing each party package and add-on

- Ensure party documents and pricing materials are visually polished and on-brand (Bauhaus-inspired, clean, colorful)

- Keep an organized image library so materials never go out with outdated or missing visuals

-Avoid any obvious AI imagery



Requirements



- Background in high-end hospitality, luxury events, or premium client services strongly preferred (hotels, private events, luxury retail, or similar white-glove environments)

- Exceptional, warm, polished client-facing communication — this person represents Highland House's premium standard to every party family

- Highly organized, detail-oriented, comfortable owning documentation end-to-end

- Comfortable with Notion (or willing to learn quickly)

- A strong eye for presentation — images, documents, and materials should always feel elevated and on-brand

-Great communication and ability to follow up with clients who reach out and answer any questions they have.

title: Credit Repair Specialist - BUREAU DIALER ONLY
description:
We help business owners fix their credit and then get approved for $50K to $150K+ in funding. Credit repair is the front door. A lot of people come to us close but not quite fundable, and your job is to get them there: cleaner reports, higher scores, the right profile, ready to fund.



We're looking for a Credit Repair Specialist to own that whole journey. You'll take someone with real problems on their report and walk them out the other side funding-ready. Right now this work lives in the founder's head, and we need you to run it better than he could.



This is not a mill where you fire off template disputes and hope. You'll manage a real book of clients and actually move their numbers, the right way.



## What you'll own



- Pull and read full reports across all three bureaus and figure out exactly what's holding the score back.

- Build a repair plan: which items to dispute, what to pay down, what to add, and a realistic timeline to funding-ready.

- Run the dispute process end to end. File it, track the bureau responses, re-dispute where it makes sense, handle validation. Follow it through the full cycle instead of firing and forgetting.

- Coach clients on the behavior that actually moves a score. Utilization, on-time payments, and not opening the wrong accounts at the wrong time.

- Track score movement and keep clients motivated through a process that takes months, not days.

- Get clients to funding-ready with a 700+ score and a clean profile, then hand them clean to the funding side.

- Keep the CRM current. If it's not in the CRM, it didn't happen.



## What we're looking for



**Read this first: this role is for experienced credit repair specialists only. Not for beginners. If you're new to credit or you're hoping to learn on the job, this isn't it, and we'll know within one question on the interview call.**



- You've read full credit reports before and you know what drags a score down and how to bring it back up. This one is non-negotiable.

- You know the dispute process and the rules around it. You work clean and compliant, and you never promise a client something you can't legally deliver.

- Familiar with CFPB, BBB, FTC, FCRA, and FDCPA.

- You're the kind of organized where nothing slips. You can carry 25 to 30+ clients at once and keep every one moving.

- Your written and spoken English is clean and professional. Clients trust you inside the first five minutes.

- You actually like working with clients. You follow up before they have to chase you.

- You're independent. Give you a goal and a playbook and you run with it. You don't need someone standing over your shoulder telling you what to do next.



## Nice to have



- Experience in funding as well as credit repair, so you understand where the client is headed after you.

- Time spent in a CRM like GoHighLevel, DisputeFox

- You've helped build or tighten up SOPs, not just followed them.



## What you get



- A real book of clients who want to be here, not a spammy cold list.

- Playbooks and templates so you're not guessing. Where they don't exist yet, you'll help build them.

- Direct access to the founder. No layers, no politics.

- Room to grow into running the whole credit side as we scale.



## How we'll measure you



You'll know exactly what winning looks like. Once you're ramped, here's what we expect:



- **Plans out fast.** Every client has a repair plan within 3 business days of onboarding.

- **Scores that move.** Clients see real, steady score improvement, and a strong share reach funding-ready inside 60 to 90 days.

- **Disputes that don't stall.** Every dispute cycle tracked and actioned on time. Nothing sits waiting on you.

- **Follow-through.** 85%+ of your clients do their part (paydowns, docs, action steps) on schedule, because you're staying on them.

- **Nobody goes dark.** Every active client hears from you at least once a week with a real update, not a "just checking in."

- **Clean handoffs.** When a client hits funding-ready, they move to the funding side with a full, accurate file. No gaps.

- **CRM stays current.** Statuses and notes updated the same day, every day. No end-of-week catch-up.



## How to apply



Send us:



- Your resume

- 2 to 3 sentences on your credit repair experience DIALING on the clients behalf AND how you handle rejections over the phone. Be specific about what you've actually done, not what you've read about.

- One example of a client whose credit you meaningfully improved, and how you did it.



Use the subject line: **"DIALER"**



Applications without that subject line or without real credit experience won't get read. We work in the details here, so show us yours.

As a Senior Web Marketing Specialist at Cybernautic, you own the strategy, execution, and ongoing optimization of SEO services that help our clients grow their organic search presence and thrive on the web.



This is not a set-it-and-forget-it role. You’ll dig into data, identify opportunities, and take decisive action on keyword strategy, content optimization, and technical SEO. Project Leadership

Systems & Process Improvement

• Support analytics and reporting system improvements



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

• Familiarity with visual or UX design concepts

BENEFITS

• Long-term engagement with a people-first U.S. agency

• Consistent schedule: Monday through Friday, U.S. business hours

• Remote/work-from-home flexibility

• Real ownership: lead SEO strategy and outcomes for U.S.-based clients

• Collaborate with a tight-knit U.S. team doing work that matters



MORE ABOUT CYBERNAUTIC

Cybernautic designs, develops, and manages the most thrilling and effective web experiences for businesses and organizations of all sizes. We’re a tight-knit team in Bloomington-Normal, IL. We believe hard work, creativity, and innovation move businesses forward — and that the web is one of the most powerful tools for making that happen. We’re looking for someone who shares that vision and wants to help shape what that looks like for our clients and our team. We know what we need and we’re passionate about finding the right fit. If this sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.

title: Hiring Senior ECommerce Video Editor ( Extra Performance Bonuses!!)
description:
About Us



We are a DTC eCommerce brand. We run paid social at a serious scale, and our creative is what separates us from everyone else in our space.



We are looking for a creative operator who understands *why* ads work, cares about performance, and takes real pride in the quality of their craft.



If you are the kind of editor who obsesses over the first three seconds, rewatches your own work to find what is not landing, this position is for you.



What This Role Looks Like



This is a **full-time, long-term position**. We do not hire editors to cycle through. We hire people we want to grow with, and we protect our best people.



**Hours:** 8 hours per day, Monday through Friday

**Output expectation:**

- 1 video per day if the project is a long-form VSL (up to 5 minutes)

- 3 videos per day for short-form ads



You will produce
 ad creative across multiple formats. You will have a clear brief, organized assets, and a team behind you. What we need from you is execution at the highest level.



What You Will Create



- Direct-response video ads built to drive purchases

- UGC-style ads that feel authentic, not produced

- AI spokesperson and presenter videos that look and sound human

- AI-generated B-roll that supports the script without looking artificial

- Motion-graphics ads with clean visual hierarchy

- Hook variations and creative iterations

- Testimonial, review-style, and listicle ads

- Product demonstrations and comparison ads



 What We Need From You



Direct-Response Editing

You understand what makes someone stop scrolling and what makes them buy. You can turn a script and a brief into a complete, conversion-focused ad. You know how to build a hook, carry tension through the video, and close with a call to action that actually converts.



UGC Editing

You can take raw creator footage and make it feel effortless. You know when to cut, when to leave imperfections in, and how to improve weak delivery without making the creator sound edited.



AI Video Production

You can use AI tools to generate or enhance spokesperson footage, voice-overs, and B-roll. You know how to catch the glitches, correct unnatural pacing, and produce an end result that does not feel artificial.



Motion Graphics and Sound Design

You can animate text, benefits, reviews, and offers in ways that aid clarity. You understand audio balancing, music selection, and how sound design affects retention.



Organization and Communication

You manage your own workload. You know what is due and when. You communicate blockers before they become problems. You submit clean, organized project files every time.



  Required Experience



- Professional video editing experience (senior level)

- Direct experience creating
 ad creative for 
 
 brands

- Experience editing UGC advertisements

- Experience producing or enhancing AI video content

- Strong motion-graphics skills (not just templates)

- Proficiency in at least one professional editing suite:

  - Adobe Premiere Pro

  - Adobe After Effects

  - DaVinci Resolve

  - Final Cut Pro

  - Capcut



**Preferred tools and platforms:** ( ALL TOOLS PROVIDED )

Kling, HeyGen, ElevenLabs, Gemini, ChatGPT, Google Drive, Slack, Meta Ad Library



    Compensation



Base: $1,500–$2,000 USD per month depending on experience, speed, quality, and communication



Performance Bonus: 0.5% of ad spend on your top 5 performing ads each month, paid after the month closes



Our top editors earn **$5,000–$7,000 per month** when base and performance bonuses are combined. That ceiling is real. We have editors hitting it.



How to Apply



**Applications are accepted by
 only.**



Send your complete application to: **[jessicahiringmanager1
.com]**



Use the subject line: **Senior Video Editor Application – Your Full Name**



Everything must be in one
. Applications missing any component below will not be reviewed. Generic, copy-paste, or fully AI-written applications that do not address your specific experience will not be considered.



---



## Application Questions



Answer every question directly in the body of your
.



**1. Experience**

How many years of professional video editing experience do you have? How much of that has been direct-response or DTC eCommerce work specifically?



**2. Output and Workload**

How many video ads did you edit in the last 90 days? How many brands or clients were you managing at the same time?



**3. Tools**

List every editing, motion-graphics, AI-video, voice-generation, and image-generation tool you actively use. Which one are you strongest in and why?



**4. AI Video**

Walk us through your process for producing an AI spokesperson video. How do you make the voice, face, and B-roll look and sound natural? What do you check before you submit?



**5. Performance and Judgment**

Tell us about a specific ad you edited that performed well or failed. What happened? What do you think caused the result? What did you take away from it?



**6. Handling a Weak Brief**

What do you do when the brief you receive is incomplete or the assets provided are not strong enough to build a good ad? Walk us through exactly what you do.



**7. Communication**

Rate your written and spoken English from 1–10 and explain your rating honestly. Are you comfortable communicating via Slack, video calls, and Loom?



**8. Availability**

What country and time zone are you in? Can you work 9-5 EST? When can you start, and do you have any current commitments we should know about?



**9. Compensation and Long-Term Fit**

What base monthly rate are you seeking?  What would you need to see from us to stay for two or more years?  Why do you want to work here specifically?



10- Commitment

Do you have any other commitments that you would need to address first? Be honest



---



## Required Work Examples



Do not send your full portfolio. Do not link a general Drive folder. Do not send work that is unrelated to this role.



Send only the following:



- **Two UGC advertisements**

- **Two direct-response advertisements**

- **One motion-graphics example**

- **One AI-assisted video**



For each example, clearly explain:

- What you personally edited, animated, or created

- What AI tools were used and where

- What stock footage, templates, or assets came from elsewhere

- What, if anything, was completed by another person



Applications that send a general portfolio instead of these specific examples will not be reviewed.



---



## Required Loom Video



Record a Loom video under five minutes, specifically for this application.



Do not send a generic introduction you have recorded for other jobs.



In your Loom:

- Introduce yourself

- Explain why you are applying to this specific brand and role 

- Walk through the strongest examples you submitted

- Explain exactly what you built in each one

- Tell us why you believe you are the right person for this position



Include the Loom link in the body of your application
.



---



Qualified applicants will be contacted by
 with next steps.

s a day

Because the support load is light, the rest of your day is store operations: editing products in Shopify, writing product descriptions, keeping the catalog accurate, and turning what our suppliers send us into finished listings.



So we're looking for a hybrid — someone who's great with customers AND comfortable in a spreadsheet and a Shopify admin panel. If you need a queue to tell you what to do next, this isn't the right fit. If you like owning a store end to end — the customers and the back office — keep reading.



------------------------------------------------------------

  • ?43,000/month to start

  • ?52,000/month after 90 days

  • That's a 21% raise in your first three months



At day 90 we review you against five things — all in your control, all tracked with

you weekly from week one:



  1. Median first response time under 20 minutes during your shift

  2. Zero unanswered DMs or comments left at the end of your shift

  3. You're handling routine questions without escalating them to us

  4. Supplier tracker current, and you flag delays before we have to ask

  5. Weekly product/listing quota met and weekly summary delivered on time



Hit those and the raise is automatic — no negotiation, no "let's revisit next quarter."The date and the five criteria go in your contract on day one, so you're holding us to it rather than the other way around.



------------------------------------------------------------



WHAT YOU'LL DO



1 — CUSTOMER CONVERSATIONS (first priority, ~3–4 hrs/day)



  • Answer Instagram and
 
 throughout your shift — target first reply

    within 30 minutes

ments: answer questions, thankhappy customers, hide and report spam and bot comments, escalate anything that needs us

 inbox: order questions, shipping, returns, exchanges, sizing, product questions

  • Look up and edit orders in Shopify: address changes, cancellations, order edits

  • Chase missing, delayed and damaged packages with the carrier, and keep the customer

    updated without them having to ask twice

  • Process refunds, returns and replacements per our SOPs; keep the returns tracker

    current



3 — ALIBABA SUPPLIER COORDINATION (~30–45 min/day)



  • Communicate with our suppliers on Alibaba and WeChat: order status, production timelines, sample requests, shipping documents

  • Follow up until you get a clear answer — polite persistence is the whole skill here

  • Maintain a simple tracker of open POs, expected ship dates and delays, and warn up  before a delay becomes a customer problem

  • Log quality issues with photos and evidence when customers report defects



4 — SHOPIFY OPERATIONS & PRODUCT CONTENT (fills the rest of your day)



  • Write product descriptions in our brand voice: clear, accurate, benefit-led, no

    fluff and no invented claims. You'll have our voice guide, the supplier spec sheet,

    and existing descriptions as models

  • Build and edit products in Shopify: titles, descriptions, images, variants, options, pricing, tags, SEO fields

  • Keep the catalog clean — fix typos and wrong specs, swap bad images, sort out inconsistent naming, tidy tags

  • Organize collections and merchandising: what's featured, what's sorted where, what's  hidden when out of stock

  • Update inventory levels and flag low stock before we sell out

  • Set up discount codes and draft orders as needed

  • Keep the FAQ and saved-reply library current from the same source

  • Basic reviews app upkeep, and write SOPs for the tasks you do repeatedly



5 — REPORTING (~15 min/day)



  • Short end-of-shift handover: what you handled, what's unresolved, what's urgent

  • Weekly summary: top complaint themes, recurring product issues, listings completed,and anything you think we should fix

------------------------------------------------------------



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



REQUIRED



  • 2+ years of customer service for an e-commerce or DTC brand — we want someone who has lived in a brand's DMs, not call center scripts only

  • Hands-on Shopify admin experience — creating and editing products, variants,

    collections, and orders. Please be specific about this in your application

  • Strong written English in two registers: conversational and warm for customer messages, clean and persuasive for product copy. We'll test both

  • Comfortable inside Instagram and
 / Meta Business Suite

  • Self-directed. With this support volume you will have open time. We need someone who fills it usefully without being told

  • Able to work 1 AM – 9 AM Manila time consistently, Monday to Friday. This is a night shift — please only apply if you've done one successfully before or are certain you can sustain it

  • Reliable computer, stable primary internet plus a backup connection



NICE TO HAVE — TELL US IF YOU HAVE IT



  • Experience messaging Alibaba suppliers or coordinating with China-based manufacturers

  • Helpdesk experience (Gorgias, Zendesk, Reamaze, Front) or ManyChat

------------------------------------------------------------



WHAT WE OFFER



  • ?43,000/month to start, ?52,000/month at 90 days on the criteria above

 your resume, a cover letter, and answers to the questions to

What You'll Own



Local SEO, the proven core of the role:



Google Business Profile setup and ongoing management across every client, correct categories, complete service info, weekly posts, and photo updates



On-page SEO: technical setup, service and location pages, schema markup, Core Web Vitals



Review systems: monitoring automated review requests, responding to reviews, growing review velocity

Citation building and consistency across directories



Local link building: outreach, placements, and relationship building with local sites and directories





AI search (AEO/GEO), the part we're building out honestly:



Structuring site content so it's clearly readable by AI answer engines, ChatGPT, Google AI Overview, Perplexity, this is mostly the same discipline as good SEO, done well



Monitoring whether client businesses actually get referenced in AI-generated answers, using citation-tracking tools, not assumptions



Reporting what's actually happening here in plain terms: what's showing up, what isn't, and why, since this channel is newer and less predictable than traditional search





Reporting, across both:



Monthly client-facing reports covering rankings, GBP performance, review growth, link placements, and AI citation tracking

An internal dashboard or tracking system so we always know exactly what's been done for each client and what it produced



What We're Looking For



3+ years of hands-on local SEO experience, ideally with home services or another high-intent local vertical

Real experience with link building and citation work, not just on-page checklists



Familiarity with AI citation tracking tools and a genuine understanding of how AI answer engines source information, not just enthusiasm for the topic



Comfortable owning reporting: you should be able to show a client exactly what you did and what changed, every month

Strong written English for outreach and client-facing reports





What Success Looks Like



Local pack rankings and organic visibility improve for assigned clients, tracked monthly

Review velocity and response consistency holds across the portfolio



A defined number of quality link placements land each month, tracked and reported, not just attempted



AI citation presence is monitored and reported honestly, improvement where it happens, a clear "not yet, here's why" where it doesn't

title: Video Editor — DaVinci Resolve (Full Time, Long Term)
description:
Full time. In-house. Long term.

Location: Remote, Philippines

Reports to: Corey, Head of Content

Compensation: $1,500 USD/month for 90 days, then up to $2,000 USD/month and beyond based on job expansion and skill



Who we are

Alive & Free is a media and education company working at the intersection of faith, emotional transformation, and coaching. Our founders teach other believers how to build coaching careers of their own.



This is an in-house role. You are not taking on a client and you are not servicing accounts. You are joining our team.



What we care about:

Trust over virality. We are building an audience that trusts, not one that clicked once

No hype and no AI slop. Our content is honest and grounded. Authenticity is at the center.

Craft is the job. We want the best looking content in our space, not content that is merely good enough



Role overview

We are hiring a full-time editor to own our long form editing department with short form layered in.

I am the Creative Director here, and you would be working directly with me.



I do not hire button pushers. I want you thinking about the work, solving problems, bringing ideas, and understanding how your edits affect performance. I set creative direction and I make the final call on it. Push me for a better idea, and then own the execution completely once the direction is set. That is the deal, and it works well when both people understand it going in.



You will work inside shared DaVinci Resolve project libraries on Blackmagic Cloud, which means I give you feedback on your actual timeline instead of vague notes on an exported file. I am a Resolve editor myself, so I will be in there with you as needed.



Responsibilities

- Editing

- Long-form video, typically 10 to 45 minutes, talking head plus b-roll. Podcasts are longer

- Short-form verticals, both pulled from long-form and produced as dedicated pieces

- Podcasts, including sizzle reel-style intros that pull the most compelling 
nts forward

- Multicam cutting for seamless flow

- VFX and motion graphics. A real requirement, not a nice-to-have

- Color and audio. Proficiency in the Resolve color page and Fairlight

- Clean project files, bins, timelines, and naming conventions

- Use of brand created and controlled assets for efficient, reproducible content

- Restructure dedicated long-form footage for retention. You will move sections, cut tangents, and build the video that should   exist if needed.



Building

- Reusable templates for captions, title cards, transitions, lower thirds, and branded assets

- Every template you build saves time on every video after it. You are helping develop the content department, not just working in it



Contributing

- Identify the strongest 
nts worth clipping for short form. I will help as needed until brand voice is recognized

- Contribute packaging ideas: titles, thumbnail directions, and angles

- Suggest improvements to flow, pacing, structure, or visual style based on what you see in the footage

- Flag weak sections before anyone asks



Solving

- Research techniques and work out how to build something you have not built before

- Use AI as a tool when it helps. We can tell the difference between using AI to solve a technical problem and letting it make editorial decisions and think for you

We will teach you our standards and goals. We are not going to teach you your craft.



Results

What success looks like:

- Long-form delivered on schedule, consistently enough that we can plan a publishing calendar around you

- Fewer than 10 revision notes in the first five minutes of a first cut by day 30

- Proposing structure rather than receiving it by day 60

- Three to five notes across a full video by day 90

- Short-form clips produced from every long-form piece

- Short-form selections we agree with without discussion

- A growing library of templates that speeds up every future video

- Clean project organization maintained across every file

- Clear communication: updates I can act on, and one good question up front instead of five along the way

- Letting me know early if you get backlogged and a solution for it

- Creative input that measurably improves the content, not just executes it

- These bars are shared with you on day one. Meeting them is what moves your compensation at 90 days.



Requirements

- Minimum 2 years professional video editing is preferred. We care far more about your portfolio than your years

- DaVinci Resolve as your primary editing software is preferred

- Portfolio including at least one long-form piece over 10 minutes

- Demonstrable VFX or motion graphics work. Fusion experience is a significant advantage. Comfort with template tools like MotionVFX counts too

- Strong eye for pacing, storytelling, and pulling out the 
nts that matter

- Ability to take feedback, iterate quickly, and deliver reliably against deadlines

- Familiarity with vertical formats for Reels and Shorts

- Character matters: Massive ownership and teachability and initiative are critical to this role.

- Excellent English comprehension. You need to hear the strongest line in an hour of talking and know it is the strongest line. That is most of this job

- Spoken English strong enough that we never have to slow down for it. I will be giving you direction and asking you questions, often quickly. I need us to understand each other the first time, without either of us stopping to decode what the other meant. If English is a strain for you in live conversation, this role will be frustrating for both of us and I would rather you know that now.

- Organized and detail-oriented, with clean file structures



Hardware and connection

- Discrete GPU with at least 8GB VRAM. 12GB or more strongly preferred. NVIDIA is preferred because Resolve is CUDA-optimized. An RTX 3060 12GB is a good reference point for what handles this work comfortably

- 32GB RAM minimum. Resolve wants this for Fusion and larger timelines

- NVMe SSD for your system and cache is preferred

- Minimum 50 Mbps upload. You will sync large project libraries daily

- A real backup plan for power and internet outages

- I will ask for screenshots of your specs and a speed test



Bonus if you have:

- Fusion depth

- Prior work in shared project libraries or collaborative editing environments

- Background in design, thumbnails, or packaging

- Experience with faith-based, coaching, or education content

- You do not need to pay for anything. We own the Blackmagic Cloud library and cover all software and cloud costs.



Rhythm

- Full time, and you must work consistent hours covering US Central standard work hours. This is a hard requirement and it is not negotiable. The way I work with you depends on live overlap. Hours that only reach US evening will not work. Please do not apply if you cannot commit to this schedule

- Exclusive to Alive and Free content. No other ongoing editing work or side gigs

- Weekly review session with me, live, inside your timeline

- Daily end-of-day update: what was completed, what is in progress, any blocks

- Heavier direction fro
 during your first several videos while I bring you into our standards



How this role grows

You are being hired to cover both long form and short form. With an emphasis on long-form as the primary skill and focus. As our content volume increases we expect to add a second editor and split the lanes so each person works to their strength. Which lane you take is a conversation we will have based on where you are strongest.



Compensation

- $1,500 USD per month for a 90 day trial. Paid weekly. Growth up to $2,000 USD per month based on performance and review after 90 days. Income can grow with this position as it expands and skill increases.

- Invite Only. $100 USD paid tryout. On completion, for every candidate who follows the full instructions for the tryout.



How the hiring process works

- Application form. REQUIRED. Experience, hardware, connection, availability, portfolio, and a short self-recorded video

- Paid tryout, by invitation only. Real footage edit test, follow up live brief, 72 hour turnaround, $100 on completion. Three deliverables: a long-form edit, a short-form vertical of your choosing, and three title and thumbnail concepts written out.

- Interview. One hour with me, talking through your edit and how you work

- Offer



To apply

- There are two steps and you need to do both.

Step 1. Apply here on OnlineJobs.ph using at least 7 Apply Points. 

Step 2. Complete this form in full: 



- The form is the real application. It is where I learn about your setup, your experience, and your work. I only review candidates who complete both steps. Partial form submissions will not be reviewed.



Applications that do not follow every instruction in this post will not be reviewed. Don't miss this incredible opportunity with a partial submission.

description:
Procurement Account Representative

McKenzie Freight Solutions LLC

About McKenzie Freight Solutions

McKenzie Freight Solutions provides procurement, logistics, and supply chain services to independently owned retailers throughout The Bahamas.

We are rapidly deploying an internal operations platform to support our procurement, pricing, warehouse, logistics, finance, and customer management workflows.

This is NOT an eCommerce website.

Our Procurement Account Representatives build customer orders over the phone by pricing the products retailers already purchase every week. The platform supports product pricing, landed costs, quotations, invoicing, supplier purchasing, warehouse coordination, logistics, customer communications, and operational reporting.

We are assembling our founding operations team and are looking for professionals who enjoy building long-term customer relationships while helping independently owned retailers reduce their procurement costs.



Compensation

Launch Sprint: $3.00 USD/hour

Ongoing Operating Rate: $4.00 USD/hour

Procurement Account Representatives who successfully complete the launch period, demonstrate excellent attendance, professionalism, communication, product knowledge, and consistently follow procedures with minimal operational errors will be eligible to transition to the ongoing operating rate following Cycle 1.

Estimated Hours

20–40+ hours during the launch sprint depending on call volume.



Immediate 48-Hour Launch Sprint

Applicants must be available to begin immediately.

We are launching a live wholesale procurement platform serving independently owned retailers throughout The Bahamas.

Training, operating procedures, call scripts, and the procurement platform will be provided before contacting customers.



About the Role

This is NOT a cold calling position.

There is no outbound cold prospecting.

Our Independent Marketing Representatives have already visited retailers in person, verified each business, and introduced McKenzie Freight Solutions.

During those visits, retailers were informed that they would be assigned a dedicated Procurement Account Representative to assist them with pricing, quotations, and their first purchase order.

You will be assigned a portfolio of retailers and will work with the same customers during recurring weekly purchasing cycles.

Your responsibility is not to pressure customers into making a purchase.

Your responsibility is to understand each customer's business, listen carefully to what they need immediately, prepare accurate product quotations, demonstrate potential savings, and build long-term procurement relationships.

You must be highly detail-oriented. Every customer conversation results in the creation of a purchase order, so accuracy in product selection, quantities, package sizes, case packs, and customer information is essential.

Value-brand alternatives

New product requests

Foodservice products

Grocery

Retail

Customer Service

Hospitality
